This document outlines the equipment inspection list I1, which must be performed 
on a monthly bases for oil cooling unit as indicated by M1 in the above titled block

The first draft is initiated by eng. Saad Samra, tested by eng. Mohamed Abdel Azeem at 27 July 2003, accepted by eng. Mohamed Elasrrag General 
Manager, revised by EDEPCo. quality control eng. Abouda El-Bana, and approved by eng. Moneer Mahmoud El Wakeel Damietta CCPS Head Sector

items: Issue work order including the teamwork names
Use Safety fences (ropes) with caution marks to surround the work area.
Wear safety helmets, shoes, earplug and gloves pairs.
Be sure that the oil-cooling unit is out of service.
Complete maintenance tool set.
Fine brushes, Compressed air hose.
Special cleaning materials (trichoroethyline).

Check the air entry side at regular 
 intervals.

Clean the cooling air entry side by 
 using fine brush.

Blow out the cooler by compressed air 
 or spray with a water jet in the opposite direction to the cooling airflow.
Be care to not distort the fins.

Use a team of jet blower with high 
 wetting agents to clean and get rid of any dirts if the cooler has a layer of 
 grease or oil. The jet should be in the opposite direction of the airflow. Dry the airside after cleaning.

Connect the oil side to a closed 
 cleaning unit with forced circulation and filter unit; use trichoroethyline as 
 a cleaning agent with 60C temperature.

Flushing should be done from both 
 sides for 30 minutes approximately.

Quantity of water [150 300 L / 
 min], pressure [3 4 bar].Check the air entry side at regular
